result.final_text:
## What this letter says
You had an appointment on 19 October 2026.
At that appointment, you agreed a plan to change your antidepressant.
The reason is side effects.
You will slowly stop sertraline. Then you will start mirtazapine.
The letter also gives the date of your next appointment.

## What you need to do
1. From Monday 26 October 2026, take sertraline 50 milligrams once a day. This is instead of 100 milligrams. Do this for 7 days.
2. On Monday 2 November 2026, stop sertraline.
3. From Monday 2 November 2026, start mirtazapine 15 milligrams. Take it once a day at night.
4. Avoid alcohol.
5. Do not drive if you feel sleepy (drowsy). Mirtazapine can make you sleepy, mostly at the start.
6. Go to your next appointment with Nurse Obi. It is on Monday 16 November 2026 at 14:00.

## Dates and medicines
Dates:
- 19 October 2026: the appointment where you agreed the change.
- Monday 26 October 2026: take less sertraline. Go from 100 milligrams to 50 milligrams once a day, for 7 days.
- Monday 2 November 2026: stop sertraline. Start mirtazapine.
- Monday 16 November 2026 at 14:00: your next appointment with Nurse Obi.

Medicines:
- Sertraline: the dose goes down from 100 milligrams to 50 milligrams. Take it once a day for 7 days. Then stop it on Monday 2 November 2026.
- Mirtazapine: you start this medicine. Take 15 milligrams once a day at night. Start on Monday 2 November 2026.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- What does the word "antidepressant" mean?
- What should I do if I forget a dose?
- What changes might I notice when I start mirtazapine?
- Who can I ask if I have questions before my next appointment?

## When to get urgent help
- Do you feel worse? Or do you have thoughts of harming yourself? Then contact the team on 01632 960 999. They are open Monday to Friday, 9:00 to 17:00.
- At any time, you can call NHS 111. Choose the mental health option.
- At any time, you can also call Samaritans on 116 123.
- In an emergency, call 999.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
